newsitem.title: UK: Coffee prices extend a rally on Vietnam talk.
newsitem.headline: Coffee prices extend a rally on Vietnam talk.

text.p: World coffee prices extended a rally on Monday, buoyed by a possibility that Vietnam may join other exporting nations in applying export curbs.
London Robusta grade March coffee futures were trading at around $1,375 per tonne, up from $1,346 at the end of last week.
News that Colombian dock workers continued a strike at the Pacific coast port of Buenaventura underpinned the market.
The work stoppage, which began last Tuesday, has caused chaos with Colombian coffee exports, more than 60 percent of which are shipped through the port.
According to the National Coffee Growers' Federation, the strike has delayed shipment of more than 160,000 60-kg bags of coffee destined for export.

In other news, Ivory Coast Minister for Commodities Guy-Alain Gauze said that Vietnam now supports the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) and will consider joining the coffee producer group.
Gauze is in Rio de Janeiro for a meeting of the ACPC on January 23 in which producers will discuss cutting exports for the January to June 1997 period.
Elsewhere in commodity markets, industrial metals either consolidated recent gains or continued a New Year rally.
Zinc rose to a new 23-month at $1,153 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange on prospects of good demand and declining stocks of the metal, used in the galvanising process.
LME flagship metal copper rebounded after early selling to trade around the middle of its recently much firmer range, going to a day's best at $2,260 per tonne.
Oil prices steadied on Monday, stemming a slide which knocked nearly $2 per barrel from the price of crude in the space of a week.
London March futures for bellwether North Sea Brent Blend were trading late in London's afternoon around $22.75 per barrel or some 25 cents firmer from Friday.
Milder weather in Europe and the United States and a steady recovery of lean heating oil stocks on both sides of the Atlantic has pulled prices down from recent six-year highs.
But stocks still remain tight.
Gold edged lower in Europe on Monday following an unspectacular end to last week and earlier dramatic falls.
Gold drifted down in the London afternoon as New York opened lower in quiet dealings. Dealers said there were few if any incentives for speculators to buy gold at present.
Gold was fixed at $353.10 per ounce in the London afternoon, down from $354.20 in the morning and 355.75 on Friday.
Benchmark Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) wheat prices were somewhat easier in early trading with the nearby March futures contract just below $3.80 per bushel.
But a move up through that level later triggered short covering by investment funds and the contract rose to touch $3.83.

Slow exports plus an estimate from the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) for Australia's 1996-97 wheat crop to total 22 million tonnes were seen as "bearish". The previous AWB estimate was for 21.5 million tonnes.
